newsitem.title: FRANCE: French welfare body estimates 96, 97 deficits.
newsitem.headline: French welfare body estimates 96, 97 deficits.

text.p: France's social security accounts commission said on Monday that it expected the welfare deficit to reach 51.6 billion francs this year and 47.1 billion francs next year, excluding exceptional measures.
The government has vowed to reduce next year's deficit to 30 billion francs and is raising taxes and excise duties to do so.
The social security accounts commission estimated last year's deficit on the welfare system, which uses payroll charges to fund healthcare, pensions and family benefits, at 67.4 billion francs.

The slight recovery in the welfare deficit would not be enough to prevent the social security accounts (ACOSS) from falling heavily into debt again, Jean Marmot, head of the social security accounts commission, said.

"The recovery is not enough to prevent the reappearance of heavy indebtedness for ACCOSS, whose cashflow needs in the coming months require urgent measures," he added in an introduction to a report on the welfare system.

The government earlier this year set up a welfare debt repayment fund, CADES, and imposed a new tax, the RDS, meant to deal with past debt and set the welfare system on a sound footing for a return to breakeven.
